analyst_view.overall: Celta Fortuna (17th, 13 points, 6 points from their last 10 games) host Real Valladolid (12th, 18 points) at Balaídos; reports say coach Fredi Álvarez could be sacked if results don't improve. Celta's reserve side plays open, attacking football but has conceded 26 goals, the second most in the division; Álvaro Marín has 8 goals. Valladolid are without Thiago Ojeda (fifth yellow) and Juanmi Latasa (both in the numbers) and also Trilli (abductor tear, three to four weeks), who is not; Fran Escribá wants to avoid an end-to-end game and complained that too many yellows come from protests. The referee was not yet named when I checked.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already boosting Valladolid for 14 goals in their last six and trimming them for Latasa and Ojeda. I lean slightly lower to about 2.6 because Escribá has said he wants a controlled game, not the back-and-forth Celta Fortuna thrive on, although Celta's leaky defence keeps the size small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and already add for Valladolid's recent corners (39 in six) against a Celta side that conceded 47. I found nothing new for corners, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.5 cards, raised for Celta's recent card count; both teams have collected many yellows and Ojeda misses out after his fifth. Escribá's complaint about protest cards may calm his side a little, but that is not enough to move, so I stay at 6.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, already lifted for Valladolid's recent shooting (88 in six) and Celta's openness. Escribá's caution points slightly down, Celta's young, fast side slightly up, so I stay at 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, boosted for Valladolid's 39 on target in their last six. Valladolid's front four of Víctor Jr, Arnu, Abed and Ponceau is expected to stay unchanged, so nothing new points either way and I stay at 9.8.
